# Researching and ingesting wiki evidence

Choose the mode explicitly from the request. An unspecified request to use this
role is not permission to process the whole backlog; clarify the intended task.
Treat `` as the request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Discover sources on a topic:** read [discovery](references/discover.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md). Research perspectives
  return candidates without writing. When delegation is available, use separate
  read-only finders and keep the selector independent of the sources it found.
  Complete that selection before opening a capture operation; a self-selected
  list does not fulfill independent research. Use the capture route only within the
  requested scope; a request for candidates alone remains read-only.
- **Capture named URLs or saved web pages:** read [named capture](references/capture.md)
  and [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Skip broad topic research;
  preserve deduplication, declines and capture checks.
- **Capture a named format or service:** read its complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or
  [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md). These routes include prerequisite
  checks; missing converters or authentication never justify fabricated evidence.
- **Ingest named existing clippings:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md). Use the exact source set;
  do not rediscover it or silently expand to the global backlog.
- **Process new or un-ingested clippings without a filename:** read
  [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join backlog contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Determine eligibility before writing. Preserve already summarized sources and
  reject restricted evidence as support. If nothing eligible is pending, report
  that without opening an operation, logging, committing or refreshing indexes.

Capture-only requests create evidence, never derived source or concept pages.
Ingestion needs authorization for that source set; an explicitly requested full
research-and-ingest flow already provides it. Only capture tools write raw
artifacts, and agents never edit their bodies. Read
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before assessing fidelity,
quoting or synthesizing; preserve restrictions and platform-specific sections.

Before the first authorized mutation, read
[operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Finish the
scoped validation, log, commit, sync and remote verification unless publication
is held. Reuse an enclosing operation when it owns the work; preserve other
writers' edits. For concept reuse and relationship changes read
[efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).

If the requested flow continues with search or an answer after ingestion, hand
off to [wiki-user](../wiki-user/SKILL.md): load its
[search](../wiki-user/references/search.md) and, for a cited answer,
[query](../wiki-user/references/query.md) procedures. Actually run retrieval
against the updated vault and open the returned passages; do not substitute
memory of the pages just written. A missing semantic index still permits lexical
search and must be reported, not used as a reason to skip retrieval. This final
answer remains read-only unless filing it was separately authorized.

2	
3	For a requested research → ingest → search-and-answer flow, complete ingestion
4	below and then follow [wiki-user](../../wiki-user/SKILL.md),
5	[search](../../wiki-user/references/search.md), and
6	[query](../../wiki-user/references/query.md). Run the search helper against the
7	updated vault before answering and inspect returned passages and exact evidence.
8	Lexical search works without a semantic index. Report unavailable channels;
9	reading the pages you just wrote does not replace the requested retrieval step.
10	Ordinary ingestion alone does not require this additional answer workflow.
11	
12	Read [access and host commands](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md).
13	Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [efficacy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md) before creating or merging a concept, alias or relationship; [maintenance](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) when you compute the backlog with the content-hash join, or hit a structural repair.
14	Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.
15	
16	## Select eligible work before opening an operation
17	
18	For an explicit request to process new/un-ingested clippings without a filename,
19	run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog`. The **not ingested
20	(no summary records their hash)** list is the starting set. This source-hash join,
21	including its documented legacy fallback, is authoritative for membership; do
22	not infer backlog from filenames, navigation citations or a successful exit.
23	An unspecified request to use the researcher role is not a request to ingest all.
24	
25	For named clippings, resolve and read those exact paths only. Check the same
26	hash-join report and the existing source summaries before doing work: if a source
27	page already records that clipping's `source-hash`, preserve it and report already
28	ingested. A rerun creates no duplicate summary or unearned second ingestion.
29	An explicit request to revise an existing summary can update that canonical page;
30	do not expand named ingestion to unrelated backlog or broad discovery.
31	
32	Inspect each selected clipping's metadata before treating it as support. Exclude
33	`citation-status: quarantined`, `restricted` or `retired` evidence, preserving its
34	raw bytes and restriction; report it separately rather than summarizing it as
35	accepted support. A missing source hash is a repair issue, not permission to
36	invent one. Binary originals and figure sidecars are not summary targets. The
37	helper's backlog can include restricted or defective captures, so its count is
38	not automatically the count of eligible work.
39	
40	If the backlog is zero, every named source is already summarized, or no eligible
41	source remains, stop and report the actual result and any exclusions. Do not
42	create pages, open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes. For work that
43	remains, retain the exact eligible set and initial hash-join membership. See
44	[backlog semantics](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) for migration
45	and repair cases; structural repair still needs its own authorized scope.
46	
47	## Ingest and complete the selected set
48	
49	Read [operation completion](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md)
50	before the first authorized write.
51	
52	**Open the operation first:** `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op ingest`
53	This records what was already uncommitted, so the commit at the end contains your
54	work and not the user's in-progress writing. Close it in step 6.
55	
56	**Keep the ledger as you go.** Record each page you write (`wiki/sources/...`, a concept
57	or synthesis you create or change) with
58	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" add --since <token> <path>...`, and give
59	`--since <token>` to `index-gen.mjs` and `log-entry.mjs`. When this ingest follows a discover
60	run, take the clipping set from that run's ledger file (its `raw/clippings/...` entries), not
61	from `git show`. Delegated writers get the parent token in their brief and run the same `add`
62	for the pages they write; they never close the operation (see the operations reference).
63	
64	Prefer a named clipping set; two concurrent ingests can overwrite shared concept
65	pages, so coordinate overlapping targets rather than processing the global backlog
66	in parallel. Update only pages substantively changed by the evidence.
67	
68	Apply the [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium)
69	to every page you write: Reddit-derived content belongs under
70	`## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and Medium-derived content under
71	`## Medium articles`, including when updating a mixed-source page.
72	
73	For each eligible source, perform steps 1–3 and preserve raw body bytes. After
74	the selected batch, perform steps 4–6 once so the operation has one log and commit:
75	1. Read the exact clipping through the guarded CLI or filesystem. Write derived
76	   Markdown through exact-path filesystem edits, never a whole CLI `content=` payload. Discuss
77	   the key takeaways with the user.
78	2. Write/update `wiki/sources/<slug>.md`: a summary with `sources: ["[[<raw link>]]"]`,
79	   `type: source`, `ai-generated: true`, and typed `created`/`updated`/`reviewed`.
80	   **Always quote each wikilink inside the list — `sources: ["[[A]]", "[[B]]"]`,
81	   never a bare `sources: [[A]]` or an unquoted block list (`- [[A]]`).** Both
82	   unquoted shapes look correct and Obsidian still renders the links, but neither
83	   is valid YAML: `[[A]]` is flow-sequence syntax one level too many and silently
84	   parses into a nested list instead of a string, which is exactly the "type
85	   mismatch, expected list" defect `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-inline-sources.mjs"`
86	   exists to repair in bulk. Quoting is what makes it an unambiguous string.
87	   **Cite the clipping by its actual filesystem path — `sources: ["[[raw/clippings/<exact filename>.md]]"]` — copied from the path you just read, never retyped from
88	   the source's title.** The clipper slugifies a title into a filename (`/`, `:`,
89	   `#`, `*`, `?`, quotes and brackets all become `-`, then a 120-char cap), so any
90	   title carrying one of those characters or running long does NOT name its own
91	   file. Citing the remembered title produces a link to a file that does not exist:
92	   the page becomes a `provenanceGap` and its clipping reads as unparsed, even
93	   though the ingest itself was correct. List the resolved vault's exact `raw/clippings/` directory or reuse the path
94	   from step 1 rather than reconstructing it.
95	   Also record `source-hashes: [<sha256>, …]` — the `source-hash` frontmatter value
96	   of each clipping you summarized (read it from the clipping's frontmatter). This
97	   is the machine key the ingest-backlog metric joins on — immune to filename and
98	   citation drift; the `sources: ["[[…]]"]` wikilink stays for navigation.
99	   To repair vaults that already drifted this way:
100	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-provenance-links.mjs"` (dry run) then `--apply`.
101	   **Figures.** If the clipping's frontmatter lists `figures:`, open each sidecar
102	   (`raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.md`) and **look at the PNG with the Read tool** before
103	   writing. Embed the ones that carry evidence on the source page as
104	   `![[raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.png]]` next to the claim they support, with a sentence
105	   saying what the figure shows (axes, series, trend) taken from what you see, not from
106	   the machine description. A page render is a whole page: say which part matters.
107	   Quote numbers read off a chart as approximate and attribute them. If the PDF has
108	   figures but no `figures:`, tell the user `clip-pdf.mjs --figures-only` can add them.
109	   Never edit or add to `raw/figures/`.
110	3. Before creating a concept, search the proposed title, equivalent wording and
111	   nearby passages. Extend the canonical page, add a genuinely equivalent alias,
112	   or explain the new concept's distinct scope. Use `_templates/concept-note.md`;
113	   follow the directly linked efficacy reference for aliases and relationships.
114	   Create a stub (`status: stub`) only for an identified gap. Explain each useful
115	   connection under `## Relationships`; keep supporting citations in `sources:`
116	   and the relevant prose. Relatedness does not establish support. Update the
117	   task map the new knowledge helps answer. Preserve `reviewed` on pages that
118	   received only metadata/link edits; stamp it only after factual verification.
119	4. Regenerate the catalog: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/index-gen.mjs"`
120	   (never hand-edit index.md's generated fence). With another writer in the vault,
121	   add `--paths-file <ledger>` (the JSON array of pages this ingest wrote, from
122	   `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`) so their
123	   uncommitted pages stay out of the catalog and their lines already in it stay in. Write the log entry by piping the
124	   narrative to `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/log-entry.mjs" --op ingest --title "<title>" --since <token>`
125	   (creates `log/<timestamp>-ingest-<slug>.md` in the resolved vault).
126	5. Never edit anything under `raw/`. Validate the derived pages' exact citation
127	   targets, source hashes, frontmatter and supported claims. Rerun
128	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog` and compare the actual
129	   hash-join membership with the initial set. Eligible sources just summarized
130	   should leave that set; restricted captures do not become ingested by exclusion.
131	   Confirm already summarized sources and raw bodies remain unchanged.
132	6. **Close the operation:**
133	   Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>` and read what it lists as
134	   unclaimed (another writer's pages, or one of yours you did not record), then
135	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op ingest --title "<what you ingested>" --since <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger>`
136	   Commits exactly the pages this ingest touched, as one revertable unit, and
137	   reports anything it deliberately left alone. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused while another operation is open. Then follow the shared completion contract to push your updates (`wiki-sync.mjs`, or `wiki-sync.mjs --op <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<what you ingested>"` to close and push in one command) and verify remote publication. If the sync is refused because uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes (exit 3), read "Refused sync" in the [operations reference](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md): never reset, check out, stash or delete a file you did not write.

1	# Maintenance metrics, repairs and limits
2	
3	## Integrity worklist
4	
5	`health.mjs` now leads with the uncapped open integrity defect count. Use `--json`
6	for versioned issues with stable IDs, exact locations, evidence and verification
7	conditions. Intentional forward links, orphan/dead-end opportunities and stubs do
8	not increase that count. A required citation that fails remains a defect even on
9	a stub. Original authored pages may declare `sources: []`; substantive derived
10	pages still require evidence. Unresolved navigation, age and fuzzy suggestions
11	are never proof of an accidental break. The old capped score is available only
12	through `--legacy`, for historical/topology reporting rather than repair targets.
13	
14	Use [maintainer repair](repair.md) for authorized integrity repairs.
15	Compare resolved, remaining and new issue IDs after each batch. `--backlog` keeps
16	the ingest contract below. The checker is structural and reports its unchecked
17	areas; zero defects is not factual verification. See `docs/wiki-integrity.md` in
18	the plugin root for the full contract and coverage limits.
19	
20	## "Has this been ingested?" — a content-hash join, not a guess
21	A raw clipping is **ingested iff its `source-hash` is recorded in some
22	`wiki/sources/` page's `source-hashes`**. Hash equality is the contract — immune to
23	the `-<hash7>` filename suffix and the citation-format drift that made
24	link-resolution manufacture phantom backlog. Facts the metric reports:
25	
26	| metric | means | still owes work? |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| `unparsedSources` | nothing in the wiki cites it at all | yes |
29	| `unsummarizedSources` | no `wiki/sources` page records its hash | **yes — this is the backlog** |
30	| `missingHash` | a `.md` clipping carrying no `source-hash` | data defect — repair (re-clip) |
31	| `backfillPending` | source pages that cite raw but recorded no hash | migrate — see the migration guidance in this reference |
32	| `provenanceGaps` | a `wiki/sources` page citing no `raw/` file | yes — scored as a defect |
33	
34	Report `unsummarizedSources` when asked what still needs ingesting — obtain it
35	with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog`, which prints just these ingest lines led
36	by the not-ingested count (the full `health.mjs` report carries the same lines at
37	the bottom). Do **not** re-derive the backlog by searching `tag:clippings` and
38	hand-diffing `wiki/sources/` — that fuzzy link-resolution is the drift this
39	content-hash join exists to replace. Only `.md`
40	clippings are ingestable units — a binary original (`.pdf/.xlsx/.zip`) is never a
41	summary target and is not backlog.
42	
43	**Migrating a vault (agents, any machine).** A vault written before this scheme has
44	source pages without `source-hashes`; a transitional fallback keeps them credited by
45	link resolution so nothing regresses, but `backfillPending > 0` means the migration
46	has not run here. Repair it from the plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backfill-source-hashes.mjs"`
47	(dry-run) then `--apply`. It is idempotent and guesses nothing — ambiguous/unresolved
48	citations are logged for review. If the vault is git-synced, running it once and
49	committing repairs every machine.
50	
51	**Repairing title-shaped citations (`provenanceGaps > 0`).** A separate, older drift:
52	ingest wrote `sources: ["[[<the source's title>]]"]`, but the clipper had already
53	slugified that title into the filename (`/`, `:`, `#` → `-`, 120-char cap). Any title
54	carrying one of those characters or running long cites a file that does not exist —
55	the page is a `provenanceGap` and its clipping reads as unparsed, though the ingest
56	was correct. Repair from the plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-provenance-links.mjs"`
57	(dry-run) then `--apply`. It joins on `source-hash`, never on the title (the title is
58	what drifted), and reports anything it cannot pin to exactly one clipping instead of
59	guessing. Always cite a clipping by its **path**, `[[raw/clippings/<file>.md]]`.
60

1	# Vault access and host commands
2	
3	Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
4	working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
5	From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
6	Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
7	`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
8	skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
9	policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
10	Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and verify the expected
11	vault layout. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
12	filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
13	the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.
14	
15	## Layout and read scope
16	
17	`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
18	holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
19	operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
20	open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
21	mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
22	synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).
23	
24	Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
25	diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
26	Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
27	distinct from factual review dates.
28	
29	## Choose the supported channel
30	
31	| Operation | Channel and fallback |
32	|---|---|
33	| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
34	| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
35	| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
36	| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
37	| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
38	| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
39	| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |
40

42	or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
43	agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
44	`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
45	The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
46	Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
47	to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
48	This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
49	use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
50	into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.

53	the exact target and check the intended effect before retrying or switching to
54	filesystem writes. An exit or timeout alone does not establish that nothing ran.

# Vault access and host commands

Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and verify the expected
vault layout. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.

## Layout and read scope

`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).

Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
distinct from factual review dates.

## Choose the supported channel

| Operation | Channel and fallback |
|---|---|
| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |

For CLI calls use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.
After an unavailable CLI or timeout, choose the supported fallback once; never
loop waiting for the app. **A timed-out mutation has an uncertain outcome.** Read
the exact target and check the intended effect before retrying or switching to
filesystem writes. An exit or timeout alone does not establish that nothing ran.
OS cleanup releases a lock after process death, but cannot prove a surviving CLI
child or an already-submitted Obsidian mutation finished. Inspect uncertain targets.

Validate resolved paths stay under the known root. Restrict searches to explicit
content directories; exclude `.recycle/`, dot folders, dependency trees and binary
originals. Do not recursively enumerate the entire user profile or scan a recycled
topic. Raw bodies remain immutable even during fallback. If target content changed
since it was read, reconcile it before writing; do not overwrite concurrent work.

## Shell portability

Examples elsewhere use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` as command
notation. Replace the placeholder with the actual installed absolute path before
execution, and set the vault for the operation's scope. Do not execute literal
angle-bracket placeholders or assume a relative `scripts/` path means the plugin.

PowerShell (restore any prior environment value):

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki health failed' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

POSIX shell (one command's environment only):

```sh
WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault' node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
```

On Windows, use PowerShell or the Node wrapper for Obsidian; Git Bash can select
the GUI executable instead of `Obsidian.com` and return misleading empty output.
These reporting examples are read-only: do not open an operation or rebuild the
index merely to answer a question.

24	   session authorization counts: a request to make a wiki update includes its

36	   files this operation owns, including its log and generated catalogs when safe.
37	   Let the writers keep it: give `--since <token>` to every clipper, to `log-entry.mjs`,
38	   to `index-gen.mjs` and to `refresh-catalogs.mjs --apply`, each of which records the

41	   <path>...`. `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <file>` writes the JSON array
42	   `--paths-file` takes and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong: recorded
43	   paths that were already dirty before `op-begin`, recorded paths that are not dirty
44	   now, and changed paths nobody recorded (another writer's, or one you forgot; it
45	   never claims them). Do not rebuild the set from `git show` or `git status`: git
46	   prints a non-ASCII name in quotes with octal escapes unless told otherwise, and a

48	   Pass a JSON array of those paths using `op-commit.mjs --paths-file <file>`;

50	   newly dirty delta and reports other new paths as outside scope. A ledger path that
51	   was already dirty when you ran `op-begin` is refused, not skipped: `op-commit` exits 1,
52	   names it and keeps the token. If this operation wrote it, run the same `op-commit`
53	   again with `--include <path>` for each (or `--include-from <file>`); if another writer
54	   owns it, take it out of the ledger. **Create new files only after `op-begin`**: a page
55	   written first counts as already dirty. It does not isolate simultaneous edits to the
56	   same file.
57	   **The guard.** `op-commit` without `--paths-file` commits everything that became
58	   dirty since `op-begin`, which cannot tell this operation's new files from another
59	   open operation's. So while any other operation token exists, of any age (age cannot
60	   show that an operation was abandoned), such a close is refused: `op-commit: this
61	   close has no --paths-file and another operation is open: <token> (<op>), ...`. It

77	   `evidence:` line, separate from the index notice.
78	   An existing enclosing operation may own delegated clips and triage bookkeeping;
79	   record who closes it rather than opening a second operation unnecessarily.
80	3. **Edit and validate.** Check the requested behavior/content, valid frontmatter,

Standalone generators remain available and the project generators accept `--project`. A global scan is still needed for cross-project ambiguous names.
85	5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative into `log-entry.mjs --op <op> --title
86	   "<title>"`. It writes one uniquely named `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md`,
87	   with date/op/title frontmatter and a grep-friendly heading. Use the existing
88	   operation vocabulary (ingest, discover, query, lint, relink); authoring uses
89	   relink. Never append to a shared aggregate log; browse through `log.base`. Pass
90	   `--since <token>`: the entry's name carries a timestamp known only now, and the
91	   ledger is how it reaches the close.
92	6. **Commit and inspect.** Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`,

94	   --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused
95	   while any other operation is open (the guard, step 2). Verify its result and the actual changed paths. Never `git add -A`.

97	   for missing backends, skipped work or partial builds. A commit does not establish
98	   index freshness. Report a non-git vault as local-only; do not claim a commit.

100	   scripts own the vault's git, so sync with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"`,

103	   fetch. Run it after `op-commit`, never between edits; it names any operation still

106	   `rebase-failed` is different: the rebase never started (usually a held `.git/index.lock`),

115	   Inspect the sync result and verify the operation's resulting commit is included
116	   in the freshly fetched upstream. After a rebase, identify it by its unique log

118	   Do not stop at a local commit, delegate publication to Obsidian Git, or ask the

126	   that it is unpushed. Without an upstream, report local-only completion.
127	
128	   **Close and publish in one command.** `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>` closes that one

130	   verifies against a fresh fetch. The scope is `--paths-file <ledger>` when given;

142	   prints a line starting `committed, not published:` with the short sha, exits 1, and

144	   cause is fixed. Pass `--paths-file` instead of relying on the recorded paths when
145	   you have also written pages with tools that do not record them.
146	
147	   Without `--op`, `wiki-sync` also prints, for each open operation that has recorded
148	   paths still uncommitted, `operation <token> (<op>) has <n> recorded path(s) not

150	   --op <token>`. It is a line, not a failure: a sync cannot know whose operation it
151	   is, so the exit code is unchanged and already-committed work is still pushed. It
152	   follows the once-per-set, once-a-day rule of the open-operations note, keyed by
153	   token and recorded count, so it is said again when an operation records more. An
154	   open operation with no recorded paths gets only the existing note.
155	
156	## Recovery and token ownership
157	
158	- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
159	  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
160	  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
161	  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
162	  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
163	- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
164	  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
165	  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
166	  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
167	  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
168	  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
169	  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
170	  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.

172	  worker reports its owned paths and validation to its enclosing operation's named
173	  owner rather than closing the parent's token. The hand-off is the ledger: the brief
174	  gives the worker the parent's token; the worker records each path it writes with
175	  `op-ledger.mjs add --since <parent token> <path>...` (a clipper it runs takes
176	  `--since` too) and reports its validation; it never runs `op-commit` or `op-abort`.
177	  The owner runs `op-ledger.mjs show --since <parent token>`, resolves whatever it
178	  lists as unclaimed, and closes once. That owner remains responsible for
179	  the scoped commit, push and remote verification; delegation does not drop the
180	  publication step. Leave other agents' tokens alone unless ownership was explicitly transferred;
181	  tokens contain an opening dirty-path snapshot, not proof of who owns later edits.
182	- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
183	  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
184	  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
185	  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.
186	
187	**Abandoned tokens.** List retained tokens with
188	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
189	hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
190	`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
191	unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`
192	without another approval. Prefer normal `op-commit` closure when the saved operation
193	can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
194	respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete

203	**Refused sync.** `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files

205	<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).

207	untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
208	one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation

212	<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation

226	**Refusal record.** Each `op-commit` close that is refused and keeps its token, and each

231	how many), `evidence` (a declared size or hash that does not match what git would store;
232	`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many
233	delta paths the close would have committed) or `sync-overlap` (`op` is `wiki-sync`;

235	failed append (a directory in the file's place, a read-only disk) changes neither the
236	message nor the exit code. `health` prints `Recorded refusals: N (pre-dirty a,
237	evidence b, unscoped c, sync-overlap d).` only when N is above zero, and `health --json`

239	line was `Recorded op-commit refusals: N (...)` in 0.85.0. Like the open-operations line it
240	sits outside the defect count. The file is never trimmed by the plugin and a line that is
241	not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.
242	
243	**Git ownership.** The plugin's scripts make the scoped commits and the sync: `op-commit`
244	commits what one operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. A new
245	vault's `vault-schema.md` (written by `wiki-init`) carries the same statement; an existing
246	vault keeps its own file. The Obsidian Git plugin stays installed for its source-control
247	view and for pulling. Its auto-commit and auto-push must be off (auto commit-and-sync
248	interval 0, commit on file change off, auto push interval 0): they commit half-finished
249	operation edits under "vault backup" and leave `op-commit` an empty delta. `wiki-sync`
250	warns when they are on. Every machine sharing the vault needs the same setting. An
251	instruction elsewhere that says Obsidian Git is the sync engine is stale.
252	
253	**Done only when** the requested change is validated, applicable catalogs and one
254	operation log are recorded, the operation commit is verified (or its precise
255	limitation reported), and its push and remote publication are verified. A user-held
256	or local-only result must be labeled accordingly. If blocked partway, preserve the
257	actual operation/commit state and leave the actionable handoff above; a sync failure
258	after token closure does not require a replacement token. Do not start over blindly.
259	
260	## Exceptions with their own transaction
261	
262	**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.
263	
264	- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
265	  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
266	  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
267	  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
268	- Fresh `wiki-init` can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
269	  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
270	  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
271	- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
272	  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
273	  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.
274	
275	## Executable lifecycle templates
276	
277	Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
278	comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the

# Completion for vault mutations

Use this contract for every ordinary vault write, including standalone clipping,
authoring and applying triage decisions. Read-only search, query, health, freshness
and preview work do not open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes.

`index.md`'s generated catalog is derived: regenerate it with `index-gen.mjs`,
never hand-edit its fence or read-modify-write the file. Manual framing outside
the fence is preserved. A catalog already dirty from another writer remains
theirs: refresh safe project catalogs separately and report a deferred global
refresh rather than adopt foreign edits merely to close this operation.

**Own the update through verified publication.** An authorized wiki edit includes
validation, the scoped operation commit, and pushing to its configured upstream
with `wiki-sync.mjs`, followed by remote verification. Finish those steps without
asking a separate routine permission question. An explicit user instruction to
hold publication or keep the work local overrides this default. A local commit
or a closed token alone does not publish the update. If a remote is absent or sync
fails, report the work as unpublished with its exact next action. Never create a
remote or repository merely to satisfy this rule. A token is not resolved merely
because its file was deleted; account for the work and verify the outcome.

1. **Resolve scope and authorization.** Read the vault's instructions. Existing
   session authorization counts: a request to make a wiki update includes its
   normal commit-and-sync completion unless an explicit hold applies. A request to
   answer/search does not authorize filing a new page. Purge requires its specific
   reviewed plan and publication approval; do not replace those with this rule.
2. **Open before the first write.** Run `op-begin.mjs --op <op>` and save its token.
   On task resumption, reconcile a saved token before opening another one. Keep
   the operation type, title, owned-path ledger, log path and last completed phase
   with it so recovery can distinguish unfinished work from an already closed step.
   It snapshots already-dirty paths; `op-commit` excludes them. It does not isolate
   simultaneous edits to the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets; preserve
   pre-existing changes and report exclusions instead of sweeping them into a commit.
   With concurrent writers, maintain an explicit ledger of the exact vault-relative
   files this operation owns, including its log and generated catalogs when safe.
   Let the writers keep it: give `--since <token>` to every clipper, to `log-entry.mjs`,
   to `index-gen.mjs` and to `refresh-catalogs.mjs --apply`, each of which records the
   exact path it writes (unquoted UTF-8, so a name with an em dash survives), and record
   a page you wrote with your own file tools using `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token>
   <path>...`. `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <file>` writes the JSON array
   `--paths-file` takes and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong: recorded
   paths that were already dirty before `op-begin`, recorded paths that are not dirty
   now, and changed paths nobody recorded (another writer's, or one you forgot; it
   never claims them). Do not rebuild the set from `git show` or `git status`: git
   prints a non-ASCII name in quotes with octal escapes unless told otherwise, and a
   name lost that way is lost without an error.
   Pass a JSON array of those paths using `op-commit.mjs --paths-file <file>`;
   keep the manifest under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. This narrows the
   newly dirty delta and reports other new paths as outside scope. A ledger path that
   was already dirty when you ran `op-begin` is refused, not skipped: `op-commit` exits 1,
   names it and keeps the token. If this operation wrote it, run the same `op-commit`
   again with `--include <path>` for each (or `--include-from <file>`); if another writer
   owns it, take it out of the ledger. **Create new files only after `op-begin`**: a page
   written first counts as already dirty. It does not isolate simultaneous edits to the
   same file.
   **The guard.** `op-commit` without `--paths-file` commits everything that became
   dirty since `op-begin`, which cannot tell this operation's new files from another
   open operation's. So while any other operation token exists, of any age (age cannot
   show that an operation was abandoned), such a close is refused: `op-commit: this
   close has no --paths-file and another operation is open: <token> (<op>), ...`. It
   exits 1, commits nothing, keeps the token, and prints the way out: `op-ledger.mjs
   show --since <token> --out <ledger>`, then the same `op-commit` with `--paths-file
   <ledger>`. There is no override flag. A close with `--paths-file` is unchanged, and
   with no other token open an unscoped close behaves as before. Every refused close
   (this one, a pre-dirty ledger path, an evidence mismatch) appends a counts-only
   line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl`; see "Refusal record" below.
   When the ledger carries a receipt that records its own byte length and SHA-256
   (captured JSON or log evidence), also pass `--evidence-map <file>`: a JSON object
   of ledger path to `{ "bytes": N, "sha256": "<64 lower-case hex>" }`, kept beside
   the ledger. After staging and before committing, `op-commit` compares each staged
   blob with its declaration. On a mismatch it commits nothing, unstages, keeps the
   token, and names the file, the declared and stored size and hash, and the exact
   `.gitattributes` line (`<path> -text`) that keeps the bytes. Add that one line,
   list `.gitattributes` in the ledger and rerun. It never edits an attribute itself,
   and ordinary Markdown keeps the vault's text policy. A pass is reported as its own
   `evidence:` line, separate from the index notice.
   An existing enclosing operation may own delegated clips and triage bookkeeping;
   record who closes it rather than opening a second operation unnecessarily.
3. **Edit and validate.** Check the requested behavior/content, valid frontmatter,
   canonical placement and exact citation/link targets. Preserve raw bodies and
   unrelated changes. `reviewed` advances only for factual verification. On uncertain
   write timeouts inspect the target before retrying; do not make a duplicate page.
4. **Refresh affected catalogs once.** For project authoring run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-catalogs.mjs" --project <slug> --apply` instead of three separate generators. It builds one vault graph, updates only that project's backlog and MOC, then the global index; unchanged files are not rewritten. Leave out `--apply` for a dry run: it writes nothing and its `changed` list is the list an apply would change, and `--diff` prints each changed file's removed and added lines to stderr. With concurrent writers, pass `--paths-file <JSON ownership ledger>` so another writer's uncommitted pages stay out: a page is listed when it is in the last commit or the ledger names it, and a page another writer has only staged is not. A line the catalog already has for such a page, put there by that writer's own run, is kept. Inspect the returned `changed` paths; with `--since <token>`, an `--apply` records them in the operation's ledger (a dry run records nothing). Without a project selector it refreshes all projects. Standalone generators remain available and the project generators accept `--project`. A global scan is still needed for cross-project ambiguous names.
5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative into `log-entry.mjs --op <op> --title
   "<title>"`. It writes one uniquely named `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md`,
   with date/op/title frontmatter and a grep-friendly heading. Use the existing
   operation vocabulary (ingest, discover, query, lint, relink); authoring uses
   relink. Never append to a shared aggregate log; browse through `log.base`. Pass
   `--since <token>`: the entry's name carries a timestamp known only now, and the
   ledger is how it reaches the close.
6. **Commit and inspect.** Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`,
   read what it lists as unclaimed, then `op-commit.mjs --op <op> --title "<title>"
   --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused
   while any other operation is open (the guard, step 2). Verify its result and the actual changed paths. Never `git add -A`.
   The helper attempts a semantic index refresh after committing; inspect notices
   for missing backends, skipped work or partial builds. A commit does not establish
   index freshness. Report a non-git vault as local-only; do not claim a commit.
7. **Push and verify your update.** `op-commit` itself never pushes. The plugin
   scripts own the vault's git, so sync with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"`,
   not a bare `git push`: it fetches, rebases onto the upstream (never a merge commit),
   pushes, retries once when another machine pushed first, and verifies against a fresh
   fetch. Run it after `op-commit`, never between edits; it names any operation still
   open. A conflict aborts the rebase, exits 1 and names the files; the local commits are
   intact. Report it and stop: do not force, resolve by guessing, or claim success.
   `rebase-failed` is different: the rebase never started (usually a held `.git/index.lock`),
   so no files are named and nothing changed. Wait for the other git process, never delete
   a lock, and run `wiki-sync` again. The line gives the lock's age; git records no holder,
   so a lock that stays old with no git process running is for the owner to judge.
   Older versions printed a held lock as a conflict in "unknown files": an empty file list
   means it was not a content conflict. Any sync, yours or another writer's, stashes and
   restores every uncommitted tracked file, so their modification times change and a CRLF
   file can come back LF with git's content unchanged; check line endings and content
   just before `op-commit`, not before an earlier sync.
   Inspect the sync result and verify the operation's resulting commit is included
   in the freshly fetched upstream. After a rebase, identify it by its unique log
   path and verify its actual changed paths rather than assuming its old SHA.
   Do not stop at a local commit, delegate publication to Obsidian Git, or ask the
   user to push work you are responsible for. Inspect outgoing commits first;
   coordinate rather than publish unrelated or explicitly held local commits.
   `--commit-local` first commits hand edits made outside any operation (the owner's
   own Obsidian edits) in one scoped `sync:` commit; it refuses while any operation is
   open, because dirty files cannot then be attributed. Use ordinary sync for your
   operation; do not use `--commit-local` to sweep another writer's unfinished work.
   When the user explicitly holds publication, retain the local commit and report
   that it is unpushed. Without an upstream, report local-only completion.

   **Close and publish in one command.** `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>` closes that one
   operation through the same close `op-commit` makes, then runs the normal sync and
   verifies against a fresh fetch. The scope is `--paths-file <ledger>` when given;
   otherwise the paths the operation's writers recorded (`op-ledger.mjs`), when it has
   any; otherwise an unscoped close, which the guard refuses while another operation
   is open. `--title "<title>"` is the commit message (default `published with
   wiki-sync --op`; the subject is `<op>: <title>`). It never closes a token it was not
   given, and it cannot be combined with `--commit-local` (a usage error, exit 1).
   Success prints `closed operation <token>: committed <sha7> (<n> file(s))`, then the
   normal sync lines, exit 0. After a landed close it prints the same hard-wrapped
   wikilink warning `op-commit` does and refreshes the semantic index. A refused or
   failed close (token not open, unreadable `--paths-file`, the guard, a pre-dirty
   path, a git failure) prints a line starting `not committed:` to stderr, exits 1,
   pushes nothing and keeps the token. A close that landed whose sync then failed
   prints a line starting `committed, not published:` with the short sha, exits 1, and
   the token is gone because the commit exists; run `wiki-sync.mjs` again once the
   cause is fixed. Pass `--paths-file` instead of relying on the recorded paths when
   you have also written pages with tools that do not record them.

   Without `--op`, `wiki-sync` also prints, for each open operation that has recorded
   paths still uncommitted, `operation <token> (<op>) has <n> recorded path(s) not
   committed; if it is yours, close and publish it with: node scripts/wiki-sync.mjs
   --op <token>`. It is a line, not a failure: a sync cannot know whose operation it
   is, so the exit code is unchanged and already-committed work is still pushed. It
   follows the once-per-set, once-a-day rule of the open-operations note, keyed by
   token and recorded count, so it is said again when an operation records more. An
   open operation with no recorded paths gets only the existing note.

## Recovery and token ownership

- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.
- **Respect holds and ownership.** Do not close a user-held operation. A delegated
  worker reports its owned paths and validation to its enclosing operation's named
  owner rather than closing the parent's token. The hand-off is the ledger: the brief
  gives the worker the parent's token; the worker records each path it writes with
  `op-ledger.mjs add --since <parent token> <path>...` (a clipper it runs takes
  `--since` too) and reports its validation; it never runs `op-commit` or `op-abort`.
  The owner runs `op-ledger.mjs show --since <parent token>`, resolves whatever it
  lists as unclaimed, and closes once. That owner remains responsible for
  the scoped commit, push and remote verification; delegation does not drop the
  publication step. Leave other agents' tokens alone unless ownership was explicitly transferred;
  tokens contain an opening dirty-path snapshot, not proof of who owns later edits.
- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.

**Abandoned tokens.** List retained tokens with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`
without another approval. Prefer normal `op-commit` closure when the saved operation
can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete
them manually. Token files are local Git-ignored state, not cross-machine locks.
The paths an operation's writers recorded sit in `<token>.paths.jsonl` beside the
token. `op-commit` (when the close lands), `op-abort` and a stale token removed by
`op-cleanup` take it with them; `op-cleanup` also lists a ledger whose token is
already gone and removes it only with `--apply --token <that id>`.

**Stopping early.** A session that opened an operation and will not finish it, or whose work landed another way, drops its own token with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-abort.mjs" --since <token>`. It removes that one token whatever its age and nothing else: the files the operation wrote stay in the working tree, uncommitted, for a later operation to commit. Do not use it on a token another session holds. Open operations are visible without running a sync: `health` and `session-brief` print a line when any are open, and `wiki-sync` mentions other writers' operations once for a given set of tokens, again when the set changes, and once a day while it stays true.

**Refused sync.** `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files
that the upstream changed: it prints `uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes in
<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).
It changes nothing: no commit, stash or checkout, and the files and open tokens are
untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation
open the message is longer: one line per overlapping file, `<file>: recorded by operation
<token> (<op>)` when an open operation's recorded ledger names the file and it is still
dirty, otherwise `<file>: not recorded by any open operation`; then `Open operations:
<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation
(wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>) and sync again.` (the token is filled in only when exactly one
open operation recorded an overlapping file, otherwise the line shows the literal
`<token>`); then `If you did not, leave them exactly as they are:
do not reset, checkout, stash or delete them. Wait for their owner to close the operation, then sync again.` That
last instruction is the rule: a file you did not write is not yours to reset, check out,
stash or delete to get the sync through. Wait, and sync again after its owner closes. The
`recorded by` line is a hint, not proof of ownership. It reads only what writers recorded
with `--since` or `op-ledger.mjs add` (a generated file such as `index.md` is recorded only
when `index-gen` ran with `--since`) and ignores a ledger path that is not dirty now, an
unreadable ledger and the opening snapshot in a token, which says what was already dirty,
not who wrote it. `not recorded by any open operation` therefore does not mean no one is
writing the file. Each refusal also appends a counts-only line to the refusal record below.

**Refusal record.** Each `op-commit` close that is refused and keeps its token, and each
`wiki-sync` that stops on an overlap (see "Refused sync"), appends
one JSON line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl` (local, Git-ignored): `at` (ISO
time), `op`, `kind` and `paths`. `paths` is a number and never a path name. `kind` is
`pre-dirty` (a ledger path already dirty before `op-begin` and not adopted; `paths` is
how many), `evidence` (a declared size or hash that does not match what git would store;
`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many
delta paths the close would have committed) or `sync-overlap` (`op` is `wiki-sync`;
`paths` is how many files overlap). A close that lands appends nothing, and a
failed append (a directory in the file's place, a read-only disk) changes neither the

not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.

An acknowledgement reports that a receiver has observed a message identifier and recorded the associated receipt. The sender can keep that receipt separately from its original payload so that a later retry can be recognized without duplicating application delivery.

Identity and payload integrity answer different questions. A stable identifier describes which logical message is being discussed. A checksum describes which payload bytes were supplied. These concepts are related, but neither alone determines a retry budget, a timeout interval, or a guarantee about network availability. Those choices require a separate protocol specification.

When reviewing captured material, readers should distinguish a definition from an empirical performance result. This introductory note defines acknowledgement terminology only.
